description: Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.

d.request: Over films with `length >= 112`, return one row: `AVG(length)` and `AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate)` (ratio computed per film, then averaged), ignoring NULLs, unrounded, NULL if no films qualify.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) AS avg_cost_to_rate_ratio FROM film WHERE length >= 112

a.request: For films whose running time (`film.length`) is at least 112 minutes, taken together as one group, what is the average running time, and what is the average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`replacement_cost` / `rental_rate`, computed per film, then averaged)? Ignore missing values in each average (giving a missing value if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) AS avg_replacement_to_rental_ratio FROM film WHERE length >= 112;

b.request: Return one row with the average `film.length` and the average of `replacement_cost / rental_rate` per film, over films with `film.length >= 112` (a film of exactly 112 minutes included), ignoring NULLs in each average, unrounded, as `(AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate))`.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) FROM film WHERE length >= 112
b.raw: Return one row with the average `film.length` and the average of `replacement_cost / rental_rate` per film, over films with `film.length >= 112` (a film of exactly 112 minutes included), ignoring NULLs in each average, unrounded, as `(AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate))`.

c.request: Using 112 minutes (`film.length`) as the cutoff for a long film, take all the long films together as one group. What is their average running time, and what is the average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate (`replacement_cost` / `rental_rate`, computed per film, then averaged)? Ignore missing values in each average (giving a missing value if none remain), return the two figures in that order as a single row, and don't round. Films whose running time is 112 minutes or more are included; a film of exactly 112 minutes counts.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) AS avg_cost_to_rate_ratio FROM film WHERE length >= 112
